sections.h2: How can I sell my Haltom City house without repairs or showings?
sections.html:
Take a cash offer for the house as it stands, or list it and handle the repairs a financed buyer's inspector will flag. Much of the housing dates from the postwar boom, so an as-is sale is a common choice for owners who do not want to put money into a house they are leaving.

The trade-off is price. A listing may bring a higher number, but it also brings repair requests, appraisal risk and a longer wait. A cash buyer pays less in exchange for speed and certainty. Ask any buyer for a written offer, the closing date, who pays title and recording costs, and whether the offer survives the buyer's inspection.

  • Pull your deed, loan payoff statement and latest tax bill.
  • List known problems: roof, foundation, plumbing, wiring.
  • Note any tenants, because their lease travels with the house.

sections.h2: What is Haltom City and where does it sit in Tarrant County?
sections.html:
Haltom City is on U.S. Highway 377 about four miles northeast of Fort Worth in central Tarrant County. The Texas State Historical Association says the town was established around World War II, with about 200 people and two businesses in the late 1940s. Within roughly ten years 5,760 people lived there, and by the mid-1960s the count had soared to 32,100.

That fast, postwar growth means much of the housing dates from the mid-twentieth century, so ask a buyer or inspector early which systems need attention. The city also built a manufacturing base: in 1976 it had thirty-five factories making goods such as sheet-metal products, clothing, plastics and fiberglass, and sixty manufacturing plants by 1990. The population was 39,018 in 2000.

Because the city sits inside Tarrant County, a Haltom City owner deals with one county clerk and one appraisal district, which keeps paperwork simpler than in cities that straddle county lines.

sections.h2: Does Haltom City require a permit for short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Yes. The city says short-term rentals must register with the city to receive a permit and operate legally, and they must also remit hotel occupancy tax. The city defines a short-term rental stay as less than 30 consecutive days, and the occupant pays the tax while the owner or operator collects it and sends it in.

ItemWhat the city states
Hotel occupancy tax rate7 percent

Source: City of Haltom City hotel occupancy and short-term rentals page.

The city uses an outside vendor to process the tax accounts, and its page lists a support line and email for login credentials. Short-term rentals are not offered any tax exemptions at this time, according to the same page. If you are selling a house that was used this way, give the buyer the permit and tax filing history so they can see what they inherit.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Haltom City house?
sections.html:
Tarrant Appraisal District handles appraisals and exemptions for Haltom City, and the district says it covers seventy-three taxing units in the county. Each unit, from the county to the city and school district, sets its own tax rate, and the district's appraisal feeds into all of them. The district also states that there is no fee to file an exemption.

Under the Comptroller's calendar, appraised values are set as of January 1, notices of appraised value for homesteads go out around April 1, and the rate-setting deadline for taxing units is late September. Bills mail around October 1. A homeowner can pay half by November 30 and the rest by June 30 of the next year if the taxing unit allows the split payment option and the owner is eligible.

Once a bill is delinquent, the cost climbs. The Comptroller lists a six percent penalty and one percent interest starting February 1, with the penalty growing one percent each month until July 1 and a collection attorney fee possible on top. A homeowner can ask the collector about a payment plan, and the Comptroller notes some collectors allow up to 36 months for a residence homestead.

  • Pay the undisputed amount while an appraisal appeal is pending, or the appeal can be lost.
  • A tax lien follows the house through a sale, so the title company pays unpaid taxes out of your proceeds.
  • Ask the Tarrant County tax office for the current balance before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What relief is there for older, disabled or veteran owners in Haltom City?
sections.html:
A homeowner age 65 or older, or disabled, receives an extra school district exemption, and the school tax on the home is frozen at a ceiling set when the owner first qualified. The Comptroller says the ceiling can transfer in proportion to a new Texas homestead if the owner moves, and a surviving spouse aged 55 or older may keep it.

Disabled veterans have a separate exemption that grows with the VA disability rating, and a veteran rated 100 percent can claim a total exemption on a residence homestead. If you are selling and buying again in Texas, ask the appraisal district how the ceiling would carry to the new address before you close.

The standard residence homestead exemption can be filed with the appraisal district, and the filing deadline is generally before May 1. A buyer who closes mid-year can often file for the rest of that tax year.

sections.h2: How do I handle a tenant or an occupant before selling in Haltom City?
sections.html:
Start with the lease. The Texas State Law Library says a landlord generally gives at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease sets another period, then files in justice court if the tenant stays. Delivery can be in person to the tenant or a household member sixteen or older, inside the premises, or by mail.

The case is set for trial between 10 and 21 days after filing. A tenant can appeal within five days of judgment, and a writ of possession can issue six days after the judgment with 24 hours' notice before removal.

For someone who moved in without permission and is not a tenant or family member, chapter 24B of the Property Code offers a sheriff or constable removal request instead of a court case, if the listed conditions are met.

sections.h2: What happens at closing and recording?
sections.html:
The title company records the deed with the Tarrant County clerk. A deed must be acknowledged before a notary or another authorized officer, and the clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, with separate records fees. Your closing statement will show the exact total.

For inherited property, the State Law Library lists four ways to put clean title in the heir's name: a transfer on death deed with the death certificate recorded, an executor's deed after administration, a muniment of title with the will, or an affidavit of heirship. The county cannot simply add an heir to the old deed. Adverse possession claims are a separate matter; a ten-year statute exists, and a claimant must show actual, visible and hostile possession, so ask a lawyer if a stranger claims your land.

faqs.q: Does Haltom City charge hotel occupancy tax on short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The city states a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax on stays under 30 consecutive days, collected by the owner and sent to the city monthly.

faqs.q: Who appraises houses in Haltom City?
faqs.a: The Tarrant Appraisal District appraises property and handles exemptions for Haltom City and the other taxing units in the county.

faqs.q: What are the penalties if I miss my Haltom City property tax deadline?
faqs.a: Taxes unpaid on February 1 draw a six percent penalty and one percent interest, and the penalty rises monthly until July 1, according to the Comptroller.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Haltom City house with a tenant living in it?
faqs.a: Yes, but the tenant's lease stays in force unless it ends or a court orders possession. Texas requires written notice to vacate, a justice court case and a writ of possession if the tenant refuses to leave.

faqs.q: How is a deed recorded when I sell in Haltom City?
faqs.a: The title company files it with the Tarrant County clerk after it is signed and acknowledged before a notary. The clerk manual lists the per-page recording fees.
